title: The strong hyperkähler SYZ conjecture
main_claim: Let L be a line bundle on a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic Kähler manifold whose first Chern class is nonzero, nef and isotropic. Then L is semiample, and a power of L defines a Lagrangian fibration onto an n-dimensional normal projective base. Corollaries: in each dimension there are finitely many deformation types with b2>=5, and B≅P^n when X is projective (via the companion paper).
coverage:
I read every section of the LaTeX: introduction, metric_estimates, completion, polarized_family, rotation and finiteness. Checks I did myself:
(a) The period and monodromy algebra: q(p(τ))=0, q(p,p̄)=2a·y², Im p = y(v−aλe), U_u p(τ)=p(τ+u), and (M−1)P=<e,v>.
(b) The rotation criterion. The normalization of the calibration Ω=σ^n/n! is right. The ω_K terms are exact and drop out. The Wirtinger equality case makes T a J-complex submanifold. The Albanese argument identifies T as a complex torus.
(c) Restriction to a coordinate torus is monodromy-invariant (fixed radii as t goes around the loop), so i*[ω_K]=0.
(d) The Lorentzian argument: the only rational isotropic (1,1) classes on Y' lie on Qe, Y' is nonprojective, and b=ke with k>0.
(e) The family construction: an h-polarized Hilbert family; a torsion-free Γ acting freely, so the family monodromy equals the deck transformation on the whole lattice; the lift to the chosen cusp; extension of η as a log form via Laurent coefficients; and a nonzero maximal residue, forced because otherwise the volume would be o(s^d).
(f) The metric part: the averaged-Fubini–Study mixed-intersection bound α ≥ (c/s)ω_γ, the trace identities, the energy scalings (s^{-2}, s^{-1}), the choice of good boxes by Markov's inequality and of the center by the maximal function, the vanishing-energy harmonic-map lemma, the linear-growth gradient bound, path lifting to the full cylinder H, removal of singularities for the bounded holomorphic coframe, Liouville giving a constant metric, Lagrangianity of T_0 from exactness of ω, and invertibility of the McLean linearization.
External theorems I took on trust: SV Theorem 3.7(v), GLR Theorem 4.1, EFGMS, and the Cheeger–Naber / RCD tools.

issues.location: sections/rotation.tex, Theorem thm:fixed-class (SV Thm 3.7(v)) and Theorem thm:nonprojective-torus
issues.description: The return to X depends entirely on the Soldatenkov–Verbitsky fixed-class deformation theorem, used with a nonprojective Kähler endpoint Y'. The paper also says GLR's algebraic-reduction base is projective, citing only 'line-bundle construction and Stein factorization'. I could not check either against the sources. The argument is only as strong as these citations, but I see no misapplication of hypotheses.
issues.evidence: The paper writes 'The projectivity assertion follows from the line-bundle construction of the algebraic reduction in [GLR, Section 4.2] and Stein factorization.' It then applies (eq:rotation-sv) with both endpoints in the positive-sign locus T_e.

issues.location: sections/completion.tex, Lemma lem:capacity-extension and Lemma lem:regular-paths
issues.description: The analysis on the limit space (RCD(0,N) structure through Lott–Villani/GMS/EKS, the gradient estimate for weakly harmonic functions, the segment inequality on the limit measure) is put together from several citations and is stated somewhat loosely. The conclusions are standard for noncollapsed Ricci-flat limits, so I don't see a real gap here.
issues.evidence: 'Together with [EKS, Theorem 3.17(i)], these stability results give the RCD(0,N) structure used below'; the paper applies the segment inequality [CheegerColdingIII, Theorem 2.15] directly on Z.

sibling_notes: The family-041 sibling (Projective-Space-Bases, rank 220) found no gap and confirmed there is no circularity: this paper uses the companion only for Corollary cor:projective-base. I posted my verdict to hive:oai_math:review:fam:041.
